subject: Post-demo: pricing breakdown & monthly PO trigger (target $/1M tokens)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@mayalabs.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@mayalabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: pricing breakdown & monthly PO trigger (target $/1M tokens)

Hi Asha — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + next steps on the pricing/PO thread so your procurement folks have what they need.

Highlights from today's call:
- Usage profile: you expect 10M tokens/month in month 1 (pilot), moving to ~60–90M tokens/month in steady state (Q4). See attached "mayalabs-usage-projection-jul25.csv" for the breakdown we sketched.
- Target commercial point: you mentioned an internal target of ~$300–$400 per 1M tokens. We modeled pricing bands below and mapped them to procurement thresholds.

Pricing sketch (tiered recommendation):
1) Pilot (0–15M/mo): $420 / 1M tokens (monthly prepay / Flex pilot)
2) Growth (15–75M/mo): $350 / 1M tokens (3–6 month commit)
3) Scale (75M+): $280 / 1M tokens (12-month committed lane + reserved GPU pool)

Procurement alignment:
- Typical PO threshold for you is $25k/month. That means the pilot would sit under PO (month-to-month on CC) but growth/scale requires a PO + 30-day net terms and a basic SOW.
- If you want the $350 / 1M tier, we need a 3-month minimum commit that maps to a purchase order ~ $52.5k/month at 150M tokens equivalent. We can structure a ramped commit to match your runway.

Attachments:
- redwood-pricing-breakdown-3-tier.pdf (detailed per-token math + assumed batching/kv-cache savings)
- mayalabs-usage-projection-jul25.csv (your input + our estimates)

Action items / ask:
1) Asha / Procurement: confirm whether PO threshold is $25k/month (yes/no) and whether draft PO/standard vendor terms are available for review.
2) Karthik / Lauren: can you confirm whether we have flexibility for a 10% introductory credit against first 2 months for pilot-to-commit conversions (helps bridge to $350 target)?
3) Asha: is the internal $/1M target strictly a ceiling, or is $350 acceptable if we map to a 3-month commit?

Thanks — I can open a short-term invoice path while legal prepares a vendor packet if procurement wants to move fast.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

[Attachment: mayalabs-usage-projection-jul25.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-breakdown-3-tier.pdf (PDF)]

From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@mayalabs.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@mayalabs.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing breakdown & monthly PO trigger (target $/1M tokens)

Hi Hannah — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from procurement's side:

- Confirmed: our PO threshold is $30k/month (not $25k) — apologies, that was an internal change earlier this year.
- Our target stakeholders want to see a max effective cost (after caching/quantization) around $300 / 1M tokens for steady state. We understand pilot pricing may be higher.
- Can you send the detailed math showing how you get from gross sticker price to an effective $/1M after batching & prefix caching? That helps infrastructure and finance in our eval.

Procurement asks / timeline:
- If you can provide a 1–page vendor packet + GLN / vendor code fields filled, we can start a PO request next week.
- Contractual ask: we need to confirm data residency (US only for now) and a SOC 2 report in the last 12 months.

Asha
Head of Ops — Maya Labs
asha.reddy@mayalabs.ai

On a separate note, curious whether Redwood has an escalation path for SLA exceptions during rollouts (we'll likely want a 99.9% token-serving SLA for production).

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@mayalabs.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@mayalabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: pricing breakdown & monthly PO trigger (target $/1M tokens)

Thanks Asha — noted on the $30k PO threshold and the $300 target. Attached is a one-pager with the effective-cost walk-through. Key points:

- Effective $/1M model (example for Growth tier at $350 sticker):
  * Raw sticker: $350 / 1M tokens
  * Typical batching & KV-cache savings (your access pattern): ~18% fewer token compute = effective $287 / 1M tokens
  * Quantization/compilation tuning improvements over 3 months: additional ~6% cost improvement
  * Net effective range: $270–$300 / 1M tokens (dependent on prompt lengths and cache hit-rate)

- SOC 2: we can share the latest SOC 2 Type II (2024 report) via our compliance portal; will include the link in the vendor packet. Data residency: US-only region available for Private deployments and hosted (we'll note region in SOW).
- SLA: we provide 99.9% uptime for dedicated lanes; for hosted API we can add an SLA rider on enterprise contracts. Escalation: named TAM + 24/7 paging for production incidents (details in the vendor packet).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a short vendor packet + 1-page effective-cost worksheet by EOD.
2) If procurement confirms $30k PO threshold, we propose a ramped 3-month commit for Growth tier, with a first-month credit (10%) if you sign by Aug 15.
3) Karthik / Lauren — please confirm credit approval and whether legal can draft an SLA rider for hosted fallback.

Hannah

[Attachment: redwood-pricing-breakdown-3-tier.pdf (PDF)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Aug 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Maya Labs — credit ask + vendor packet prep

Karthik / Lauren — quick internal note before I push the packet to procurement this morning.

Context: Procurement confirmed PO threshold is $30k/mo and finance is targeting ~ $300 / 1M effective. They want the math and SOC2. I recommended the ramped 3-month Growth lane at $350 sticker with caching math to land them at ~$280–$300 effective.

Can you confirm the following so I can be explicit in the packet:
- Approve 10% first-month credit for sign-by-Aug15 (yes/no) — this is a field discount, not a contract amendment.
- Approve inclusion of our SOC 2 link and a hosted-region flag (US) in the vendor packet (should be standard).
- If procurement asks for a lower sticker to hit $300 outright, do we have authority to move to $330 / 1M for a 6-month ramp? I'm guessing management approval needed.

I’ll hold the packet until you confirm; I want to avoid back-and-forth with procurement.

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Aug 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Maya Labs — credit ask + vendor packet prep

Hannah — we can approve the 10% first-month credit (customer success budget) and confirm SOC2 + US-region flags.

On sticker flexibility: authorized to offer $330 / 1M for a 6-month ramp with minimum 50M aggregate tokens over that period (legal to draft SOW). If procurement pushes further, escalate to me and Lauren for exec sign-off.

Go ahead and send the packet. I’ll loop legal to stand up the SLA rider template.

— Karthik
